title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Future Harm Exception to Confidentiality
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A client, enraged after losing an LTB hearing, screams in the paralegal's office, "I am going to drive to my landlord's house right now and shoot him!" and the paralegal believes the threat is genuine. Under the LSO Paralegal Rules of Conduct, what is the paralegal's duty?
options: The paralegal may disclose the confidential information to prevent the crime involving death or serious bodily harm.
The paralegal is strictly forbidden from disclosing this information under any circumstances.
The paralegal must seek the client's written consent before calling the police.
The paralegal must report the adjudicator to the LSO for triggering the client.
questions.explain: Under Rule 3.03(4), a paralegal *may* disclose confidential information, but must not disclose more information than is required, when the paralegal believes on reasonable grounds that there is an imminent risk of death or serious bodily harm, and disclosure is necessary to prevent the death or harm. Note: In Ontario, the rule uses "may" (permissive).
